summary: Auric’s exhausted residents are already turning against refugees when a mixed Verge–Shard evacuation ship arrives under fire, forcing Halev to spend his government on people he cannot house.
settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — REFUGEE BERTH AND CIVIC DOCK — NIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: Closer to the heater. I’m not asking twice.

dialogueInline.speaker: Boy
dialogueInline.text: You’re cold too.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: So are nine thousand voters, and they want this berth closed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: They can tell me themselves.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: They may have to shout. We have an unscheduled ship coming in loud.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Cargo?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: People. Verge and Shard. Several hundred, if the life signs are honest.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: We cannot house them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Open the berth.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: That may be the last order this government obeys.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Then make it useful.

panelPlan: Wide: Auric’s beautiful market ring is dimmed by rationing; displaced families sleep beneath shuttered stalls while residents argue across a portable heater queue.
The Luminara Mother gives the Boy her place near the heater as Wallace shows Halev a petition demanding the refugee berth be closed.
Jex interrupts with a broken distress transmission: an unscheduled evacuation ship, carrying both Verge and Shard civilians, is approaching inside the supply convoy.
Wallace warns there are no beds, heat reserves, or votes for this; through the canopy, distant weapons fire flashes around the crippled ship.
Halev orders the berth opened. Dock crews move while Wallace quietly says this may end Halev’s government; Halev watches the ship burn toward them.
directionInline: Keep Auric visibly exhausted before the crisis arrives: rationing, sleeping families and a heater queue should already be consuming the public space. Halev's final order must happen while the burning evacuation ship is physically visible, so the political cost and the immediate human need occupy the same frame.

summary: Inside the crippled evacuation ship, Dr. Richard Secundo abandons the bridge to keep a mixed group of enemies alive while his son Paul inherits control of a vessel coming apart.
settingText: EVACUATION FREIGHTER MERCY OF DAWN — PASSENGER HOLD

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Hold that brace. Both of you. Push together.

dialogueInline.speaker: Shard Caregiver
dialogueInline.text: Give the mask to the kid.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: You need it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Shard Caregiver
dialogueInline.text: She needs it more.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: Dad, the bridge is draining our reserve. I can keep pressure here or there. Not both.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Can you route control to your slate?

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: It’s a repair slate.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Can you do it?

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: Yes.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Vent the bridge.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: What if someone’s still up there?

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: I checked. It’s empty. Save the hold.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: Control transferred. Dad—something’s cutting through the hull.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Keep us moving. I’ll handle the breach.

panelPlan: Hundreds of Verge and Shard civilians pack a freight hold as a pressure door bows inward; adults from both factions brace it with cargo poles and their bodies.
Richard treats a wounded Shard caregiver who pushes their last oxygen mask toward a frightened Verge child.
Paul reports from an exposed engineering crawl that the bridge can retain pressure or the passenger hold can—there is not enough power for both.
Richard looks toward the distant bridge, then orders Paul to vent it and transfer control to his repair slate; he is terrified and obeys.
The lights stabilize for one breath. Cutting torches ignite on the outer hull beside the children; Richard tells Paul to keep them moving.
directionInline: Treat the passenger hold as a failing workplace, not a tableau of suffering. Richard keeps moving while he triages; Paul is separated from him in engineering and communicates through broken systems. The Shard caregiver's sacrifice is practical and quick, with no sentimental staging.

summary: Billie converts Abby’s cargo raid into a political atrocity, while Tess realizes grievance has become an excuse to punish civilians.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Containers only. Do not touch the passenger hull.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: The Fleet left our families outside the cordon.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: These people did not do that.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: No. But the Fleet came for them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Billie, pull your people back. That ship is not the target.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: I know. I changed the target.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raider
dialogueInline.text: I can hear children inside.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Do not lock onto that ship.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Our children froze outside that cordon. Lock us on.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Call Venn. Tell her we are boarding the civilians she came to save.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Gravefire, come about. We are going after Ashfang.

panelPlan: Through Ashfang’s canopy, supply containers separate from the crippled refugee ship; Abby’s order marks the containers while Billie marks the passenger hull.
Tess challenges the changed target over comm as boarding crews load weapons; Billie shows an old image of Shard families frozen outside a Fleet cordon.
Abby orders Billie back to cargo. Billie argues the mixed ship will expose Fleet mercy as selective and cuts Abby’s channel.
A raider hesitates at the boarding collar after hearing children through the hull; Billie personally slams the collar forward.
Ashfang bites into the passenger section while Gravefire turns away from the cargo prize and follows.
directionInline: Billie's escalation should be visible as a change of target on the tactical display before anyone names it. Abby, Tess and Billie are not delivering faction positions; they are fighting over an order in real time while boarding hardware is already moving.

summary: Ordered to protect authorized cargo and treat the refugees as a threat, Venn knowingly trades her command for the burning ship.
panelPlan: Thunderbreak’s luminous bridge shows two crises: exposed medicine and heater cargo on one side, the refugee freighter being boarded on the other.
Dominion appears by holo and orders Venn to hold the authorized supply screen; the mixed evacuees are labeled an infiltration risk.
Tactical explains that diverting leaves Auric’s supplies open. The officer quietly tells Venn Dominion’s order is logged.
Venn asks the bridge to identify anyone receiving the refugee distress call; every station light answers. She orders the turn.
Exterior: Thunderbreak leaves the cargo screen and dives through wreckage toward Mercy of Dawn as raider fire begins walking across its hull.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: You are authorized to protect the supply convoy, not that ship.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: They are transmitting civilian registries.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: They are also transmitting Shard codes. Stay with the convoy.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: If we leave, the medicine convoy is exposed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: Dominion’s order is logged, Commodore.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: You all hear that distress call?

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: Yes, Commodore.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Do not turn Thunderbreak.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Helm, take us to the freighter.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Venn.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Auric, cover the convoy as long as you can. We are going for the civilians.

directionInline: Keep the two losses visible at once: exposed medicine and heater cargo on one side of the bridge picture, civilians under boarding fire on the other. Venn's turn should read as a command decision made after hearing the same distress call as everyone else, not as a heroic pose.

summary: Naomi prevents Fleet rescue from becoming Fleet occupation, and Venn proves trust by surrendering control when command would be easier.
settingText: VERGE ESCORT — COCKPIT / THUNDERBREAK RESCUE BAY

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Mercy of Dawn to anyone. Boarders are through the outer hull.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: My rescue team launches in forty seconds.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Not if Fleet marines go in first. Half that ship will fight you before they know you came to help.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: If we wait, there may not be a ship left.

dialogueInline.speaker: Second
dialogueInline.text: Captain, the voice on that channel was my father.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: We go in first. Verge shuttle, Fleet medics. Keep the rifles down.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: My officer is leading the rescue.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: If a Fleet officer leads, they may not open the doors.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Officer, Captain Sol has the lead.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: Commodore?

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: You heard me. Move to support. Launch.

panelPlan: Naomi sees Fleet marines loading in Thunderbreak’s rescue bay while Richard’s broken transmission identifies frightened Shard and Verge families together.
Naomi tells Venn armed Fleet control will make half the ship resist rescue; Venn argues that waiting will kill them all.
Naomi’s second receives a broken voice fragment from a parent aboard; the personal connection makes the cost of getting the rescue posture wrong immediate.
Naomi demands operational lead and Verge markings on the first shuttle. Venn removes her own officer from the lead seat and grants it publicly.
A small shuttle carrying Naomi, Verge crew, Fleet medics, and unraised weapons launches into fire; Venn remains behind, answerable for Naomi’s choices.
directionInline: Naomi's objection is operational, not rhetorical: rifles and Fleet markings are the problem she can solve before docking. Venn should visibly remove her own officer from the lead seat so the transfer of control is a concrete act of trust.

summary: With one shuttle load left before the ship breaks, Naomi sends the children away and stays behind with the adults she cannot promise to save.
settingText: MERCY OF DAWN — FRACTURED PASSENGER HOLD

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: One load left. It can take the children or some of the wounded. Not both.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Children first.

dialogueInline.speaker: Child
dialogueInline.text: Not without her.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: She can’t walk.

dialogueInline.speaker: Child
dialogueInline.text: She gave me her air.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: Dad, the crack is opening again.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Put her in my seat.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: That leaves you here.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: I know. Get them aboard.

dialogueInline.speaker: Junior Rescuer
dialogueInline.text: Captain, I can’t leave you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: You can. Get those kids out. Seal the hatch.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Who here can still work?

panelPlan: Naomi’s team enters a hold divided by a widening structural crack; one rescue shuttle remains docked while hundreds press toward it.
Richard explains the shuttle can carry the children or a smaller mixed group of injured adults, not both; the hull has minutes.
A Verge child refuses boarding without the wounded Shard caregiver who gave up an oxygen mask; panic threatens the transfer.
Naomi puts the caregiver aboard in her own place, gives command of the shuttle to a junior rescuer, and seals herself, Richard, Paul, and the remaining adults inside.
Through the closing window, children reach for parents as the shuttle departs. Naomi turns back to the failing compartment and asks who can still work.
directionInline: The shuttle capacity problem must be readable without dialogue. Naomi gives up her own restraint for the caregiver and is physically left behind when the children depart. Let the closing hatch carry the emotional beat before she turns back to work.

summary: Tess disables one of her own raiders to protect a refugee, then seals the breach beside Naomi as both women cross a faction line they cannot uncross.
settingText: MERCY OF DAWN — RAIDER BREACH / PASSENGER HOLD

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Put the medicine down.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raider
dialogueInline.text: Billie said strip the hold.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: I heard her. Put it back.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: That case keeps twelve people breathing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raider
dialogueInline.text: They can move.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: You first.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Step away from him, Tess.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Fine. Help me with the breach.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: I’m not turning my back on you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: You don’t have to. Hold the plate.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Tess, you’re helping them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: I’m stopping a leak.

panelPlan: Tess enters through Ashfang’s smoking breach and finds a raider tearing medical packs from Richard while the pressure patch fails behind them.
Tess orders the packs returned. The raider invokes Billie and raises a weapon toward a refugee who tries to intervene.
Tess strikes first, pinning and disarming her own crew member; Naomi arrives with her weapon trained on Tess.
The breach splits wider. Naomi and Tess lower their weapons simultaneously and brace a patch while Richard pulls civilians clear.
The seal holds. On Billie’s monitor, Tess is unmistakably visible working beside Naomi; Billie orders Tess away from them, and Tess keeps working the breach.
directionInline: Tess's break with Billie begins as a small physical refusal: return the medicine, stop the raider, hold the failing plate. Naomi and Tess lower their weapons because the air leak becomes more urgent than deciding whether they trust each other.

summary: When the refugee ship splits from the supplies Auric needs to survive, Venn chooses the people in front of her and forces Halev to bear the people who may die later.
settingText: THUNDERBREAK — BRIDGE / AURIC CIVIC CONTROL / MERCY OF DAWN

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: The spine is separating. We can hold one section, not both.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: We have three hundred people back here. Take the passenger section.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: That spine has heat for nine thousand people and antibiotics for the fever ward.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: I have patients who will not survive another impact.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: And I have patients who will not survive the week.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Venn, choose.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Lock the tractor on the passenger section.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: That cargo is heat and medicine. People are going to die without it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: I know.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Understood. Auric clinics, revise intake. We just lost a week of supplies.

panelPlan: Mercy of Dawn breaks into a passenger section and a supply spine as luminous debris closes; Thunderbreak’s single tractor field cannot hold both.
Naomi calls from the passenger hold while Richard supports failing patients; the tactical display counts hundreds of life signs there.
Halev appears beside Auric’s dark rings and names what is in the other section: heat for North Ring and antibiotics for the fever ward.
Venn refuses both Naomi’s demand and Halev’s arithmetic for one silent beat, then locks the tractor onto the passenger hull.
Thunderbreak pulls the people clear while the supply spine drifts toward debris. Halev orders Auric’s clinics to prepare for what will now be missing.
directionInline: Keep the split ship and the two incompatible rescue targets on the same tactical picture. Venn's silence before choosing the passenger section should last long enough for both Naomi's and Halev's costs to remain valid.

summary: Jex gives up the hidden passage that made him powerful because a partial secret would send Tess and Auric’s supplies to their deaths.
settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — VEIL MARKET BACK ROOM

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: You have a route to the supply spine.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: I have one nobody else knows.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: What will it cost?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: My clients. Three safe houses. Every favor tied to that route.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: I have nothing left to give you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: I know.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Will you open it?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Send Gravefire the first marker.

dialogueInline.speaker: Scribe
dialogueInline.text: That is not enough. They will hit the shear at the second turn.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Open the whole route. Every marker.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: You will never own it again.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: I know.

panelPlan: Jex watches the supply spine drift toward destruction on a route table while his private Veil passage glows beneath layers of locked seals. The route table is explicitly technical: timing windows, shear markers, anchor fixes, and the second turn required to stay inside the usable reciprocal gradient; it must not read as mystical cartography.
Halev asks for the route; Jex names the clients, safe houses, and years of leverage that open transmission would expose.
Halev has nothing left to buy the route with and asks Jex directly whether he will open it anyway.
Jex offers only the first marker; the scribe calculates that Tess will enter blind and die at the second turn. Jex removes every seal.
The full passage erupts across public channels. Jex’s waiting clients destroy their route tokens as Tess turns toward the revealed path.
directionInline: Jex's route is technical leverage, not mysticism. Show the hidden passage as timing windows, shear markers and anchor fixes while the list of clients and safe houses makes clear what he is surrendering by opening it.

summary: Naomi and Tess carry the severed refugee ship and its supplies through a spectacular broken-moon passage while Paul must trust his father to disappear from view.
settingText: THE SHATTERWAKE — MULTI-LOCATION INTERCUT: REFUGEE PASSENGER HULL / SUPPLY SPINE / GRAVEFIRE / THUNDERBREAK

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Paul, bring our nose toward the blue fracture.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: It keeps moving.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Watch the blue edge. It’s moving slower than the rest.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Paul, keep your eyes on the slate.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: I can’t see your section.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: I’m working. You keep flying.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Thunderbreak will not fit through.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Take the long way around.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: We’re already turning.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: The supply spine is slipping. I’m going to push it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: You’ll tear Gravefire apart.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Maybe. Get Paul through.

panelPlan: Panel 1 — exterior establishing shot; no faces or shared interior: luminous fragments of a shattered moon rotate inside a violet nebula. Naomi’s small Verge escort shepherds the severed passenger hull; Gravefire braces the loose supply spine; Thunderbreak stops at the passage mouth because the cruiser cannot fit. Show ordinary realspace distorted by rotating fragments and damaged corridor geometry shifting the local reciprocal gradient; no hyperspace tunnel, portal, or mystical passage effect.

Panel 2 — supply-spine engineering blister; Paul is the only physically present named character. He straps himself beside exposed machinery and steers from his repair slate. A small navigation display shows Naomi’s Verge escort beside the distant passenger hull. Dialogue in exact order: Naomi over bordered radio balloon, ‘Paul, bring our nose toward the blue fracture.’ Paul, ‘It keeps moving.’ Tess over a differently styled radio balloon, ‘Watch the blue edge. It’s moving slower than the rest.’ Do not show Naomi, Tess, or Richard in this compartment.

Panel 3 — supply-spine engineering blister; Paul remains the only physically present named character. His small comm screen shows Richard working over patients inside the separate passenger-hull medical hold. Dialogue in exact order: Richard through the screen, ‘Paul, keep your eyes on the slate.’ Paul, ‘I can’t see your section.’ Richard through the screen, ‘I’m working. You keep flying.’ Rotating moon fragments eclipse the passenger hull, and Richard’s image breaks into static. Do not put Richard physically beside Paul.

Panel 4 — Thunderbreak bridge; Venn is the only physically present named character, framed against the passage the cruiser cannot enter. Dialogue in exact order: Venn, ‘Thunderbreak will not fit through.’ Naomi replies through a bordered radio balloon, ‘Take the long way around.’ Venn, ‘We’re already turning.’ Do not show Naomi on Thunderbreak.

Panel 5 — Gravefire cockpit; Tess is the only physically present named character. A gravity pulse pulls the supply spine away as Tess drives Gravefire bodily against it. Dialogue in exact order: Tess, ‘The supply spine is slipping. I’m going to push it.’ Naomi answers through a bordered radio balloon, ‘You’ll tear Gravefire apart.’ Tess, ‘Maybe. Get Paul through.’ Do not show Naomi inside Gravefire.

Panel 6 — exterior closing shot; no dialogue and no group portrait: Naomi’s escort and the passenger hull disappear through one luminous gap while Gravefire pushes the supply spine carrying Paul through another. Far behind them, Thunderbreak turns alone toward the pursuing raiders. The ships’ separation must be unmistakable.
directionInline: Preserve strict spatial separation between passenger hull, supply spine, Thunderbreak and Gravefire. The page works only if Paul's inability to see Richard and Thunderbreak's inability to enter the passage remain visually unmistakable.

summary: Abby publicly chooses the refugees and her sister over Billie, splitting the Shards and turning a political disagreement into a broken intimate loyalty.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Break your lock on Gravefire.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Your sister chose the refugees.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Tess chose people you were about to kill.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: They were dying in front of me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: You’re turning on us for Venn?

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: This is not about Venn. You boarded a civilian ship.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Move, Abby.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: No.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: You won’t fire.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Try me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Abby—

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Go.

panelPlan: Ashfang lines up on Gravefire as it shoves the supply spine; Abby’s smaller skiff crosses between them while Shard captains watch on open comms.
Billie turns Tess’s rescue into a test of whether Abby will choose her sister over Shard unity; Abby refuses the framing and points to the civilians Tess protects.
Billie accuses Abby of turning on the Shards for Venn; Abby refuses the frame and points back to the civilian ship Billie chose to board.
Billie advances. Abby fires across Ashfang’s bow, scorching its armor; the watching skiffs divide into two formations.
Ashfang withdraws behind its supporters. Tess continues into the passage without thanking Abby; Abby remains between both camps, having lost half her fleet.
directionInline: Abby's warning shot should divide the watching Shard ships before anyone knows which side will hold. Do not stage Abby as triumphant; she is losing political unity while choosing the civilians and Tess.

summary: Thunderbreak fights alone at the passage mouth, and Venn makes a frightened junior officer choose rescue over a clean act of revenge.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: Three salvos inbound. Point defense is saturated.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Launch the drones. Push the missiles into the debris.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: I have a clear shot on the cutter that hit Luminara.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: If you fire, what loses power?

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: The tractor.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: And the passenger section?

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: It falls back into the debris.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: If you keep the tractor?

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: The cutter gets away.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Your call.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: Dropping the shot. Power to tractor.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: Impact—brace!

panelPlan: Epic exterior: Thunderbreak holds the narrow mouth against Billie’s skiffs, armor shining under impacts while refugee sections disappear behind it.
On the damaged bridge, Venn opens defensive drones like a luminous fan to bend missiles into rotating moon debris.
A junior officer finds a clean shot on a retreating Shard ship responsible for an earlier civilian strike and asks permission to take it.

The same power can fire or preserve the failing tractor field protecting the last passenger section. Venn makes the officer state exactly what loses power and what happens to the civilians if the shot is taken.
The officer drops the solution and feeds the tractor. Thunderbreak takes a brutal hit, but the last civilian hull clears as bridge lights fail.
directionInline: The junior officer's firing solution should look genuinely cleaner and easier than maintaining the tractor. Venn does not give the answer; she makes the officer state the consequence of each use of the same power bus.

summary: Auric residents try to divide the arrivals by faction until the Luminara Mother gives part of her own berth to the Shard caregiver who saved a Verge child.

dialogueInline.speaker: Resident
dialogueInline.text: Shard arrivals stay behind the red line.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Do not split my patients by faction.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: Chris, this berth is about to riot.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: I know.

dialogueInline.speaker: Child
dialogueInline.text: She gave me her air.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: How many in your family?

dialogueInline.speaker: Shard Caregiver
dialogueInline.text: Two. If my sister made it off.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: We have one berth. You can take half.

dialogueInline.speaker: Boy
dialogueInline.text: They can use my blanket.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: That does not make room for hundreds.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: No. Remove the partitions anyway.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: You can start with that one.

panelPlan: The severed passenger hull opens into an overwhelmed concourse; wounded Verge and Shard families emerge together beneath improvised faction barriers.
Residents demand that Shard arrivals be searched and separated. Wallace tells Halev the crowd will not accept them in the existing berth.
Richard refuses to let medics split mixed family and care groups; the wounded Shard caregiver arrives beside the Verge child saved earlier.
The Luminara Mother recognizes what happened, removes a barrier herself, and offers half of her family’s tiny berth to the caregiver.
Others begin moving barriers while some residents turn away in anger. Halev orders all faction partitions removed and accepts the unrest.
directionInline: Keep the improvised faction barriers physically present until civilians begin removing them. The Mother's choice should start local and material—half a berth, one blanket—before Halev turns it into policy.

summary: Dominion offers Venn her command in exchange for separating Shard refugees from their families; she refuses and removes her insignia before her crew.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Detain every Shard arrival. Verge nationals may disembark after screening.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: There are mixed families.

dialogueInline.speaker: Keating
dialogueInline.text: Classification is not punishment.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: It is when the door locks.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Captain Sol’s rescuers will also submit to inquiry.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: They just brought the children through.

dialogueInline.speaker: Keating
dialogueInline.text: Officer, remember your station.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Ella. Carry this out and you retain command.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: And Fleet relief continues if I do it?

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Yes.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: No.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Officer, log my refusal. I am relinquishing command pending tribunal.

panelPlan: Emergency lamps illuminate Thunderbreak’s scarred bridge while Auric receives mixed families; Dominion and Keating appear over a fractured holo table.
Dominion orders all Shard arrivals detained and Naomi’s rescuers surrendered for questioning, presenting compliance as the only way to preserve Fleet relief.
Venn asks whether children and mixed households will be separated. Keating says classification is not punishment; an officer reacts despite trying not to.
Dominion privately offers Venn continued command if she executes the order. Venn removes her star insignia and sets it beside the damaged route display.
The holo vanishes. Some crew salute; others stare at dead consoles and the stranded cruiser, frightened by the cost of following her.
directionInline: Venn's insignia should remain on the damaged console after Dominion's transmission ends. The bridge crew reaction must be mixed: respect, fear and uncertainty rather than a unified salute to rebellion.

summary: Unable to house the refugees without breaking mixed families, Halev opens Auric’s unsafe luxury ring and makes enemies of the traders who kept him in power.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: The Crown Ring is sealed for a reason.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: The window is dangerous. The rest is bonded property.

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Your plan splits twelve families and breaks up every care group from the ship.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: The fracture monitors still answer. Barely.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Can we monitor the crack all night?

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: If somebody stays with it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Clear the bonded stores. Move the families together.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: The owners financed your coalition.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: They can be angry. I need the rooms.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: They will end this government.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Open the door.

panelPlan: Halev, Wallace, Richard, and Paul stand before the sealed Crown Ring: elegant empty apartments curve around a spectacular cracked observation window while refugees crowd outside.
Wallace explains that the ring is structurally suspect and its suites hold bonded goods belonging to the traders who support Halev’s coalition.
Richard rejects the alternative allocation plan because it separates mixed households and care groups; Paul finds the fracture monitors are old but responsive.
Halev orders the stored luxuries removed and families admitted under continuous watch. Wallace tells him the owners will bring down the government.
Doors open onto the gorgeous failing habitat. Refugees enter carrying almost nothing as repair crews—including Paul—move toward the glowing crack.
directionInline: The Crown Ring should look desirable and unsafe at the same time: luxury finishes, bonded goods and a spectacular cracked window. Halev's decision is not opening an empty palace; it is accepting structural risk and political retaliation to keep families intact.

summary: Naomi accuses Venn of making a heroic rescue whose aftermath the Verge must carry; their partnership survives only after Venn stops defending herself and leaves Auric practical support she can still authorize.
settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — SERVICE AIRLOCK OVERLOOKING THUNDERBREAK

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: You saved them. Now Auric has no relief, no room, and half a Shard fleet coming after us.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: I know.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: No. You get to leave. We are the ones who have to live with what happens next.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: You’re right.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: That’s all you have to say?

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: No. But you’re still right.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Will Thunderbreak still be yours tomorrow?

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Probably not. Before they remove me, I can transfer the rescue drones to Auric and give your controllers everything they need to coordinate with Thunderbreak.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Verge command. Civilian oversight. No Fleet base. Not now, not later.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Agreed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: I’m still angry.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: You should be.

panelPlan: Naomi finds Venn alone in a service airlock, watching damaged Thunderbreak beyond Auric’s glass while refugee traffic moves behind them.
Naomi lists the consequences landing on Auric: lost Fleet relief, divided residents, exposed defenses, and hundreds with nowhere durable to live.
Venn says she knows what Auric is carrying now; Naomi rejects that as insufficient because Venn can still leave while Auric lives with the consequences.

Venn admits Naomi is right and reveals she may no longer control Thunderbreak tomorrow; while she still has the authority to do it, she offers to transfer Thunderbreak’s rescue drones to Auric and provide the operational data needed for local controllers to coordinate with the cruiser.
Naomi sets strict terms—Verge command, civilian oversight, no permanent Fleet presence. Venn accepts, and they turn together toward the work.
directionInline: Naomi must be allowed to stay angry after Venn agrees with her. Keep refugee traffic and damaged Thunderbreak visible behind them so the argument remains about who carries consequences after a dramatic rescue. Venn's offer must read as a limited operational handoff she can still authorize before being removed from command, not as giving away protected Fleet weapons, command codes, or permanent military control.

summary: Billie takes a civilian tug hostage and demands Tess, forcing Abby to choose openly between her sister and the unity of the Shards.
settingText: AURIC APPROACH — REFUGEE SERVICE TUG / SHARD COMMS

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Auric, I have one of your service tugs.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: Dad—if you hear this, I’m on the service tug. We’re losing air.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Send me Tess and I stop venting the tug.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: I’m coming out.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: No.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: She has civilians.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: She wants you. Walking out there does not save them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Choose, Abby. Your sister or your people.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Tess is one of my people. So are the civilians on that tug.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: You could lose every captain you have left.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: If they leave over this, let them leave.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Any ship still with me, target Ashfang.

panelPlan: Ashfang clamps a civilian service tug carrying repair workers and oxygen cylinders beside the inhabited Crown Ring; Billie broadcasts across Auric.
Paul, aboard after joining the window repair crew, hides beneath machinery and reports that Billie has begun bleeding atmosphere.
Billie demands Tess surrender, arguing that Abby must choose her traitorous sister or the Shards she claims to lead.
Tess prepares to launch alone. Abby physically blocks Gravefire’s hatch and tells her dying for Billie will not save the hostages.
Billie opens a vent valve remotely. Frost blooms across the tug windows as Abby orders every captain still loyal to her to attack Ashfang.
directionInline: Billie's leverage is the venting tug, not her speech. Abby physically stopping Tess from surrendering should make the sister relationship active in the scene before Abby turns the remaining Shard captains against Ashfang.

summary: Fleet, Verge, and rebel Shard rescuers save the hostage tug together while Abby defeats Billie but chooses civilian lives over revenge.
settingText: AURIC CROWN RING — HOSTAGE TUG / ASHFANG BATTLESPACE

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Thunderbreak, roll between them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: We may not be able to recover.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: We only need to do it once.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Paul, the manual valve is aft of the oxygen rack.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: The rack is coming loose.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Stay low. I’m cutting Billie’s remote control.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Abby sent you?

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: No. Paul needs air.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Ashfang’s guns are dead. Billie is launching.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Let her go—I’m losing the tug!

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: I’m coming. Brace for contact.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: Valve shut. We have air.

panelPlan: Full-energy opening: Ashfang fires past Abby’s skiffs toward the hostage tug; crippled Thunderbreak rolls between the shot and Auric’s luminous Crown Ring.
Naomi grapples the venting tug with her escort while Paul crawls through freezing machinery to reach the manual valve.
Tess breaches Ashfang’s boarding collar and cuts the remote vent control; Billie attacks her inside the narrow industrial passage.
Abby disables Ashfang’s firing assembly and has Billie’s escape pod in her sights, but Naomi calls that the tug is tearing free with people aboard.
Abby abandons the shot and braces the tug beside Naomi. Billie escapes; Paul closes the valve, and mixed civilians pull one another toward returning air.
directionInline: Crosscut the rescue so every faction contributes a different capability: Thunderbreak absorbs fire, Naomi holds the tug, Paul reaches the valve, Tess kills the remote control and Abby abandons a revenge shot to brace civilians. Do not collapse the action into one hero.

summary: Auric survives without resolving its fractures: refugees gain a precarious home while every leader faces the political cost of saving them.
settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — CROWN RING OBSERVATION GALLERY — MORNING

dialogueInline.speaker: Richard
dialogueInline.text: Your hands need another hour before you touch a tool.

dialogueInline.speaker: Paul
dialogueInline.text: The window can’t wait an hour.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: They put my route on the public board. They spelled it wrong.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Correct it. Publicly.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: You’re enjoying this.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Civilian command, mutual rescue, no permanent Fleet base.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: And when the Fleet asks who authorized it?

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Tell them I agreed to it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Tell them Auric authorized it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Boy
dialogueInline.text: Are we staying here?

dialogueInline.speaker: Mother
dialogueInline.text: For tonight.

dialogueInline.speaker: Boy
dialogueInline.text: That’s longer than yesterday.

panelPlan: Morning over Auric: the Crown Ring’s enormous cracked window frames a radiant planet and damaged ships; refugees and residents repair the gallery together.
Richard checks Paul’s frostbitten hands while he insists on returning to window watch; the Mother and Boy share breakfast with a Shard family.
Jex finds his once-secret passage copied on public repair slates; Halev receives notice that his coalition has withdrawn support.
Venn receives a tribunal summons as Naomi presents Halev with a civilian defense accord—Verge command, shared rescue obligations, no permanent Fleet base.
The Boy asks whether the gallery is home. His mother answers, ‘For tonight,’ as former enemies raise one transparent repair panel into the stars.
directionInline: End on unfinished stability. Repairs, political notices, shared breakfast and the new civilian-defense terms should coexist in the same morning. The Boy's final question works because the adults have solved only tonight.
